title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
text:
Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

 From New York via Montana

 Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G

 Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

 Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

 Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and pathos-drenched, loping forward like an aimless but essential winter morning walk.

 While Stillwater captures the spirit of 70s singer-songwriter piano ballads, the rest of Eiger’s forthcoming record is rangier and harder to pin down, touching on traditional folk and loose, minimalist prog. It is undoubtedly the best of his projects to date, and is sure to be one of the year’s breakouts, if recent successes by sharp-tongued songwriters such as Cameron Winter and This Is Lorelei are anything to go by. Shaad D’Souza
